knowledge_units.context_summary: Tumor PD-L1 promotes lung metastasis by engaging myeloid PD-1 to suppress type I interferon signaling, rather than directly inhibiting CTLs. This mechanism represses Cxcl9 and Cxcl10 expression, impairing CTL recruitment to metastatic sites. The study identifies a specific signaling axis linking tumor PD-L1 to metastatic progression via myeloid cell modulation.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Tumor PD-L1 does not affect primary tumor growth or initial lung colonization efficiency but promotes lung metastasis by suppressing CTL-mediated clearance. This effect requires a functioning adaptive immune system and is mediated by a third factor present in the lung metastatic niche. Single-cell RNA sequencing of lung leukocytes revealed that PD-L1 loss drives transcriptional changes specifically in myeloid cells, including enhanced antigen presentation machinery in macrophages.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Tumor PD-L1 (tPD-L1) suppresses type I interferon signaling in myeloid cells via PD-1 engagement, rather than directly inhibiting CTLs. This suppression reduces MHC class II expression and IFN-beta production, creating an immunosuppressive niche that impairs CTL recruitment to lung metastases. Depletion of myeloid cells abolishes the pro-metastatic effect of tPD-L1.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study extends findings to human patients with metastatic basal cell carcinoma, showing that PD-1 blockade releases myeloid differentiation restriction and enhances interferon signaling. The discussion highlights that tumor PD-L1 (tPD-L1) does not directly suppress CTL activation but instead binds to myeloid PD-1 (mPD-1) to create an immunologically cold metastatic niche. This mechanism distinguishes tPD-L1's role in metastasis from its potential sufficiency but not necessity in primary tumor response to PD-1 blockade.
